findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
The following TCS food items were observed to be out of temperature: 

1. There were 76 bottles of lemonade that were probed to be at temperatures between 57F and 62F. These bottles of lemonade state to “Keep Refrigerated” and were placed in a open-air unit that did not allow proper cold holding. All of these bottles were voluntarily discarded by the PIC. 
2. There are multiple containers of cut cantaloupe and cut watermelon that were observed to be placed on top of ice for cold holding. The ambient temperature of these containers of watermelon and cantaloupe were between 55F and 60F. The PIC voluntarily agreed to place these containers of cut TCS fruit on Time as Control and these containers will be sold or discarded by 5pm.

Ensure that TCS food items are being properly cold held at 41F and below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
The following equipment is observed to be in need of repair: 

1. The gasket on the walk-in freezer in the back storage area across from the entrance to the back by the meat coolers is observed to be cracked. Ensure that this gasket is replaced. 
2. The gasket on the door of the freezer holding Caulipower frozen pizzas and the gasket on the door of the freezer holding Johnsonville breakfast sausage (both in Aisle 11) are both cracked and need replaced. 
3. There is ice build-up in the walk-in freezer labeled “Bakery Freezer” by the alcohol section. Ensure that this issue is repaired and the ice is removed. 

Ensure that equipment is maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

findings.comment: A cooler holding cut fruit (watermelon, pineapple, etc.) was observed to be holding at a temperature of 74.5F. CORRECTED-The fruit was voluntarily discarded by the PIC. Discussed with PIC the importance of holding TCS foods under 41F.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: A cooler holding cut fruit (watermelon, pineapple, etc.) near the front of the store was observed to be above 41F (74.5F). The fruit was voluntarily discarded by the PIC. A follow up is scheduled for 5/28/2025 to ensure that the cooler has been repaired and is properly cold holding TCS items (41F and under).
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
There were small containers of eggs and cartons of eggs that were observed to be stored above Frank’s Redhot Sauce in a dairy cooler. The facility was attempting to fill space due to a current egg shortage. CORRECTED- Educated PIC that raw eggs cannot be above Ready-to-Eat foods, such as the Frank’s Redhot Sauce. This storage order was corrected during the inspection. 

There was also meat from the meat department on a box of salmon in the cooler of the seafood department. CORRECTED- The meat was removed from the cooler and the operator was unsure why it was in the cooler. Educated PIC on proper storage order.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: There was black soil residue accumulation on the sides of the ice machine in the seafood area. Discussed this with the PIC. A follow up is scheduled on 3/17/2025 to ensure that this has been cleaned. Food contact surfaces should be clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
The following food items were observed to be available for purchase past their sell by date: 

1. Multiple jugs of Prairie Farms Lactose Free Whole and Reduced Fat Milk dated sell by 3/5/2025. 
2. 4 containers of Oscar Meyer Chicken Breast lunch meat dated sell by 3/5/2025. 
3. 5 containers of Oscar Meyer Turkey Breast dated sell by 2/11/2025. 

All items were discarded and operator was educated on the importance of discarding food that is past its sell by date.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.18: There were 4 containers of Prairie Farms Lactose Free Skim Milk that expired on 11/16/2024 that were still available to be sold. CORRECTED- These containers were discarded and the staff was educated. The operator stated that this type of milk does not typically sell well and it was just missed, as the date for milk is checked while it is stocked or being faced correctly. It was recommended to check all the dates daily to avoid this issue in the future. Ensure that all food is discarded if it exceeds the manufacturer’s expiration date. 

(A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
The seafood 3 door cooler was observed at a temperature of approximately 50F. The fish and shrimp in the cooler were observed at a temperature of 46-50F. The seafood worker stated she put the fish and shrimp in the cooler around 8:00am this morning, and the cooler was empty at the start of the day. The contents of the cooler were moved to the deli walk in cooler. Also, a note was placed on the cooler instructing staff not to use the cooler until it maintains a temperature below 41F. 

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.comment: 6-501.16: Observed wet mop head to be stored in mop bucket. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment: 2-301.14: Observed food employee in seafood department put on new gloves without first washing hands.  Wash hands whenever new gloves are worn. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: 4-602.11: (A) Observed shovel used to put ice in seafood display cooler to only be washed, rinsed and sanitized every few weeks per seafood department employee.  Advised employee that food contact surfaces should be washed, rinsed and sanitized every 4 hours.  Shovel was washed, rinsed and sanitized during inspection. FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned before each use, each time there is a change in work, between uses of raw FOODS to RTE FOODS, before using FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE, and when contamination has occurred. (C) Cleaned at least every 4 hours.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment: 6-403.11: (A) Observed Pepsi can on food contact surface of meat cutting table.  Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation
Observed magnetic knife strips in the produce and meat rooms to be in disrepair with varying degrees of rust on the magnets.  Repair or replace the magnetic strips in produce and meat rooms.
findings.citation_text: 4-201.11  (C) In-use equipment and/or utensils in disrepair. Remove from use and replace with equipment that is durable and easily cleanable meeting National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI standards. Reference 4-201.11.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
750.510 & 160 - Employees in produce room were observed putting on gloves to cut produce without first washing hands. Handwashing and glove use were discussed.  

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time they may have been contaminated, before putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.
findings.citation_text:
750.530 - Employee in meat room was chewing gum while cutting meat. Gum was discarded at request of inspector. 

Employees shall consume food, including gum, only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.citation_text:
750.530 - Powerade bottles (one empty and one containing beverage) were observed inside one of the label machines in the meat room. Bottles were discarded during inspection.

Store personal beverages properly in designated areas/break room.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
750.650a - Magnetic knife strips in the produce and meat rooms were observed to be in disrepair with varying degrees of rust on the magnets. Repair or replace the magnetic strips in produce and meat rooms. 

Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.citation_text:
750.830 - Meat room did not have a set of test strips for checking sanitizing concentration. Obtain and use quat test strips.

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text:
750.860 - Clean cutting board was observed behind the faucet at the seafood area 3 part sink. Potential for exposure to splash and cross contamination were discussed. Cutting board was moved to proper clean equipment storage area.

Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.citation_text:
750.1300 - Spray bottle with a generic "all purpose" label was not labeled as to the contents. Bottle was observed hanging form a pipe adjacent to the water heater outside the door to the produce room. A gentleman in the back was asked if he knew what was in the bottle. He sprayed the liquid on his hand and smelled it. Worker noted it appeared to be some sort of oil. Bottle was removed from the area to be verified as to the contents or discarded if contents could not be verified. 

Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.
